books.section: A. The Ascendancy of the New Right
Reagan, H. W., Clinton, and W. (1980-2001)

stem: Why did the Iran-Contra affair become a major scandal for the Reagan administration?

options.text: Reagan publicly announced the arms sales in a televised address
options.misconception: The sales were secret; they were exposed by investigation, not announced by Reagan.

options.text: Officials secretly sold arms to Iran to fund the Contras
Congress had voted to give the Contras unlimited military aid
options.misconception: Congress had limited aid to the Contras; the secret funding defied those limits.

options.text: The Contras refused to accept any American aid at all
options.misconception: The Contras welcomed the aid; the scandal was how the money reached them, not whether they wanted it.

rationales.A: Background: the sales were secret; they were exposed by investigation, not announced by Reagan.
rationales.B: Background: officials sold arms to Iran in violation of a trade embargo and used the money to aid the Contras, defying congressional limits on that aid.
rationales.C: Background: Congress had limited aid to the Contras; the secret funding defied those limits.
rationales.D: Background: the Contras welcomed the aid; the scandal was how the money reached them, not whether they wanted it.
rationales.general:
1. Follow the money in the passage: weapons to Iran, cash to the Contras.
2. Background: the arms sales violated an official trade embargo with Iran.
3. Background: the Contra funding defied limits Congress had placed on aid to the rebels.
4. Nothing here was public, unlimited, or refused — the secrecy and the defiance made it a scandal.
Remember: secret arms, embargo broken, Congress bypassed — that is the scandal.

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of 5 Steps to a 5 2024, Chapter 28, and Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 11. Post-1929 material is paraphrased, not quoted.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of an account of the Iran-Contra affair: In the mid-1980s, Reagan administration officials secretly sold weapons to Iran, despite an official trade embargo, in order to win Iranian help freeing American hostages held in Lebanon. They then used the money from those sales to aid the Contra rebels fighting Nicaragua's Communist-leaning government, defying limits Congress had placed on aid to the Contras. When the scheme was discovered, Congress held nationally televised hearings.
